conditions.field.name.tip: Identifies this condition in the table and in the pipeline's skip/failure log messages — useful for debugging which condition decided the result when there are several. Optional: left blank, an automatic summary is shown instead.
conditions.field.left.tip: Interpolated text (accepts {{VAR}} from env/parameters and dynamic tokens like {{$timestamp}}). E.g.: {{TOKEN}}, {{EXPIRES_AT}}.
conditions.field.right.tip: Compared against the value on the left. Use {{$timestamp}} for 'now' (epoch seconds). Ignored for Exists/Doesn't exist.

settings.shortcut.next_tab.desc: Selects the next folder tab, wrapping around from the last back to the first.
settings.shortcut.previous_tab.desc: Selects the previous folder tab, wrapping around from the first back to the last.
settings.shortcut.edit_item.desc: Opens the editor for the currently selected item in the tree.
settings.shortcut.delete_item.desc: Deletes the currently selected item in the tree (with confirmation).
settings.shortcut.quit.desc: Actually quits Kai (unlike the window's X button, which only hides it).
settings.shortcut.toggle_search.desc: Shows or hides the search bar, focusing it when shown.
settings.shortcut.context_menu.desc: Opens the context menu for the selected item, navigable by keyboard.
settings.shortcut.focus_output.desc: Focuses the Output panel's input field, or returns focus to the tree if it's already focused.
settings.shortcut.toggle_edit_mode.desc: Switches an open editor dialog between Simple and Advanced (JSON) mode.
settings.shortcut.edit_folder.desc: Opens the editor for the current folder/tab.
settings.shortcut.edit_body.desc: Opens the quick body editor for the selected command.
settings.shortcut.stop.desc: Stops the selected command's running process.
settings.shortcut.force_stop.desc: Force-kills the selected command's running process.
settings.shortcut.reset.desc: Clears the failed/error state of the selected command.
settings.shortcut.expand_selected.desc: Expands the selected folder in the tree.
settings.shortcut.collapse_selected.desc: Collapses the selected folder in the tree.
settings.shortcut.expand_all.desc: Expands every folder in the tree.
settings.shortcut.collapse_all.desc: Collapses every folder in the tree.
settings.shortcut.hide_selected.desc: Hides or shows the selected item, folder, or collection.
settings.shortcut.hide_window.desc: Hides the main window, same as the X button — only while the window itself is focused (not global, and never while typing inside an interactive terminal). Different from the global show/hide hotkey below, which works even when Kai isn't focused.
settings.shortcut.show_hidden.desc: Toggles whether hidden items are shown in the tree.
settings.title: Global Settings
settings.window.auto_hide.tip: Launcher behavior: clicking outside hides Kai to the tray, so the global shortcut always brings it back with a single press. Requires a system tray.
settings.output.auto_collapse: Collapse the Output when selecting folders and collections
settings.output.auto_collapse.tip: Folders and collections have no output: the Output collapses by itself and reopens when you select a command. If you collapse or open it by hand, your choice wins.
settings.window.start_visible.tip: Decides visibility when Kai opens, without depending on the global shortcut: on, always visible; off, always hidden (tray only). On by default (more predictable — global shortcut registration can fail for reasons outside the user's control, e.g. a WSL/WSLg environment or a collision with another app already using the same combination). Reopening with it off is still possible via the tray icon or `kai show` (CLI).

cli.usage.banner: Kai CLI — runs commands by CLI path and controls the running Kai.
cli.usage.label: Usage:
cli.usage.section.paths: CLI Paths (commands with a cli_path; local when the folder has a kai.json/kai.yml):
cli.usage.paths_discover: kai [path...]                 lists the available paths (the root, or inside a folder)
cli.usage.paths_run: kai <path...> <args>          runs the command (required args positional, optional --name=value)
cli.usage.paths_global: kai -g <path...>              uses the app's global paths even with a local file (or --global)
cli.usage.paths_detached: kai -d <path...> <args>       runs in the background and hands the terminal back (combine: -gd)
cli.usage.paths_window: kai -gw <path...> <args>      also opens the output in its own window (or --window; needs -g)
cli.usage.run: kai run <command-name>        runs a command by name
cli.usage.env_use: kai env use <name>            activates an environment
cli.usage.import: kai import [file|folder]      imports the kai.json/kai.yml as a project (no argument: current folder)
cli.import.not_found: No kai.json, kai.yml or kai.yaml in '%1'.
cli.import.unsupported_file: '%1' isn't a project file — use kai.json, kai.yml or kai.yaml.
cli.raise.no_tray: No system tray in this environment: the notification was only added to Kai's history.
cli.usage.raise: kai raise [--level <level>] <msg>  notification in Kai's tray (info, warning, error)
cli.usage.validate: kai validate <file>           checks a kai.json/kai.yml for structural errors
cli.usage.completion: kai completion <bash|zsh|powershell>   prints the shell autocomplete (Tab) script — e.g. eval "$(kai completion bash)"
cli.usage.ps: kai ps [--json]               lists the running processes
cli.usage.attach: kai attach <pid|name>         follows a process's output live (Ctrl+] releases the terminal)
cli.usage.history: kai history [N] [--json]      latest runs recorded by Kai
cli.usage.last: kai last [--log] [--json]     the most recent run (--log shows its output)
cli.usage.init: kai init [--json] [--force]   creates a kai.yml here from the detected project
cli.usage.paths_flags: flags: -g global · -d background · -n notify when done · -w output window · --dry-run · --json (combine: -gdnw)
cli.attach.hint: Following — Ctrl+] releases the terminal without stopping the process.
cli.attach.detached: Terminal released; '%1' keeps running in Kai.

cli.error.not_running: Kai is not running (could not connect to IPC). Open Kai first.
cli.error.usage.env: Usage: kai env list | kai env use <name>

command_editor.render_markdown.tip: Renders the accumulated Output as formatted Markdown (headings, lists, links, code blocks) instead of plain text — with scrolling and search. Takes priority over Formatted output if both are checked.

kip.cli.help:
kai kip — helper for programs that speak KIP (Kai Interface Protocol).
Prints ONE protocol message per call on stdout. Pure and offline: no Kai app needed.

Usage: kai kip <verb> [options]

Verbs:
  hello    [--title T] [--version V]
  prompt   --id ID [--title T] [--description D] [--submit-label L] [--back] [--no-cancel] [--no-remember]
           --field <type> <name> [label] [field options]   (repeat --field for more fields)
  confirm  --id ID --text TEXT [--title T] [--danger] [--confirm-label L] [--cancel-label L] [--back] [--no-cancel]
  patch    --id ID --seq N [--field ...] [--remove name[,name]] [--chip ... | --no-chips]
  chip-result <chip-id> <running|success|error> [text] [--title T] [--id PROMPT]
  invalid  --id ID [--error field=message]... [--message TEXT]
  message  [info|success|warning|error] TEXT
  markdown TEXT | --file PATH
  progress <0-100|null> [label] [--no-cancel]
  steps    --id ID [--title T] --item ID [label] [--state S] [--detail D] ...
  step     <steps-id> <item-id> <pending|running|success|error|skipped> [detail]
  table    [--id ID] [--title T] --column key:label ... --rows-json '[...]'
  notify   TITLE [TEXT] [--level L]
  set-env  NAME VALUE
  done     [--title T] [--text X] [--level L] [--action type:label:value]... [--path-format F]
  raw      '<json>'          validates a KIP message and prints it
  get      '<json>' <path>   prints a value from a response (e.g. values.env, values.opts.dry)

Field types: text secret textarea number date select list table filepick folderpick flags
Field options (apply to the LAST --field):
  --required  --default V  --placeholder T  --description T  --group G  --watch  --no-remember
  --options a,b,c  --option value:label[:description]  --multiple (list/table)
  --min N  --max N  --step N  --decimals N (number)   --mode date|time|datetime  --range (date)
  --flag name:label[:default] (flags)   --column key:label  --row-key K  --rows-json '[...]' (table)
  --filter '*.sql'  --initial-dir DIR  --path-format native|posix|windows (filepick/folderpick)
  --search  --no-search  --page-size N (list/table: filter box and pages of N items)
Chips (prompt/patch; the --chip-* options apply to the LAST --chip):
  --chip ID [label]  --chip-description T  --chip-icon NAME  --chip-danger  --chip-requires field[,field]
  --chip-confirm  --chip-confirm-title T  --chip-confirm-text T  --chip-confirm-label L  --chip-cancel-label L
Before the first --field, --description and --no-remember belong to the prompt itself.

Exit codes: 0 ok · 1 get: path not found · 2 invalid usage (message on stderr, nothing on stdout).

command_editor.kip.tip: Runs the command as a KIP app: the program talks JSON Lines over stdout/stdin and Kai shows forms, confirmations, progress and results as native screens instead of terminal text.
command_editor.kip_window.tip: Shows the KIP app in a separate window instead of the output panel.
command_editor.kip.hint: Kai never changes your command: add the flag your tool needs (for example --kip) yourself. Features that compete for stdin/stdout (interactive terminal, formatted output, auto-responders, background, schedule…) are turned off while KIP is on; "Exportable variables" stay available for set_env.

settings.kip.hint: KIP (Kai Interface Protocol) lets a command show forms, progress and results as a native screen. These are the global preferences; whether a command uses KIP is set in its own editor (shell commands only). Writing a KIP program with an AI assistant? Help → AI manifestos copies the guide with one click.
settings.kip.handshake_timeout: Wait for the program to introduce itself
settings.kip.handshake_timeout.hint: If the program prints no valid first message (hello) in this time, Kai stops it and shows "This command doesn't support KIP". Raise it for slow starts (WSL, containers).
settings.kip.change_timeout.hint: After you change a field that updates others (watch), the form stays locked until the program answers. After this time it unlocks again and logs a warning.
settings.kip.cancel_grace.hint: Cancel asks the program to quit. If it is still running after this time, Kai stops it.
settings.kip.remember_answers.tip: Pre-fill each prompt with what you answered last time (never passwords). A program can opt out per prompt or field.
settings.kip.expand_details: Open Details when a command fails
settings.kip.expand_details.tip: Show the log and the protocol inspector on failure screens. Off keeps them collapsed until you open them.
settings.kip.clear_remembered.tip: Removes the remembered answers of every KIP command. Takes effect immediately.

command_editor.kip.remembered.hint: Kai pre-fills each question with what you answered last time. Forgetting applies when you press OK. Turn this off for every command in Settings → KIP.
command_editor.kip.forget.tip: Clears the answers remembered for this command.
command_editor.kip.variables.hint: A KIP program can hand a value to other commands (for example a login token) with set_env, but only for names declared in the Exportable variables tab.
command.field.language.tip: Native runs the text as a shell line/script (the default). Python and Node treat it as code: Kai hands it to the interpreter without any shell quoting.
command.field.interpreter.tip: Optional: overrides the global interpreter (Settings → Languages) for this command only. It is a shell line resolved where the command runs, so it can have arguments (e.g. uv run python); quote paths with spaces.
command_editor.language.hint: This is %1 code: Kai hands it to the interpreter as-is, so {{VAR}} is NOT replaced here. Variables and parameters arrive as environment variables (%2). Output is unbuffered and UTF-8. The `kai` module is injected too: notifications, environments and processes of the Kai app.
command_editor.language.export_excluded_: Python and Node commands can't export variables to Kai this way (use KIP's set_env).
command_editor.kip.module_hint.python: Python: the kip module is injected — just `import kip` (kip.prompt(...), kip.progress(...), kip.done(...)). The code runs without a shell, so stdin stays free for Kai's answers.
command_editor.kip.module_hint.node: Node: the kip module is injected — use the global `kip` (or require('kip')) with top-level await (await kip.prompt(...), kip.done(...)). The code runs without a shell, so stdin stays free for Kai's answers.
settings.languages.hint: Python and Node commands run through these interpreters. Each value is a shell line resolved where the command runs — on a WSL target it is the WSL's python3, and a login shell already loads pyenv/nvm — so you usually don't need to change anything. It may have arguments (e.g. uv run python); quote paths with spaces. A single command can override it in its own editor.
settings.languages.python.tip: Default: python3 (python on Windows without a terminal target). E.g. ~/.venvs/tools/bin/python
validate.warning.language_capture_env: 'capture_env' has no effect on python/node commands — they can't export variables to Kai (use KIP's set_env).
validate.warning.interpreter_without_lan: 'interpreter' only applies when 'language' is python or node — it is ignored on this command.
